object_types.name: Vendor
object_types.definition: A supplier from which the business can procure goods or services. Identified by a vendor number assigned at creation.

source_references.excerpt: The vendor record. It's the thing in the supplier master... Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.
Every vendor has exactly one, and no two vendors share one... It's the thing we quote in every conversation with AP.

object_types.name: VendorNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to a vendor record upon creation.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created... It's the thing we quote in every conversation with AP.

object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The operational status of a vendor: draft (initial state), active (approved for transacting), or suspended (temporarily blocked).

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended... It defaults to draft the moment the record is created.
Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

object_types.name: LegalName
object_types.definition: The registered legal name of a vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Legal name. Tax ID. Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

object_types.name: TaxID
object_types.definition: The tax identification number of a vendor. Not unique as a vendor identifier, as the system contains duplicate vendors sharing the same tax ID.

source_references.excerpt: Could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?... You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: The spending category assigned to a vendor based on procurement volume: bronze (default/low spend), silver (medium spend), or gold (high spend with enhanced terms and support).

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold... Gold vendors are the ones we spend real money with, they get quarterly business reviews, better payment terms, a named relationship manager.
Every vendor gets a spend tier. Bronze by default if nobody's assessed them.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: The risk classification assigned to a vendor based on compliance review: low, medium, or high, based on factors such as data sensitivity, geographic scope, and sole-source status.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high... based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A compliance assessment of a vendor's risk profile. Each review is a distinct record with its own identifier, reviewer signature, and timestamp. A vendor accumulates multiple reviews over time; at most one is marked current and is required for the vendor to be in active status.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one.

object_types.name: ReviewID
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a risk review record.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: Region
object_types.definition: A geographic region for vendor operations and contact assignment. Currently four regions exist: EMEA, APAC, NA (North America), and LATAM.

source_references.excerpt: What identifies a region?... Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM... Four regions, fixed? Four today.

object_types.name: RegionCode
object_types.definition: The code identifying a geographic region.

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.

object_types.name: Contact
object_types.definition: A vendor contact name for a specific region.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.

source_references.excerpt: A purchase order has a PO number. That's its identifier, same idea as vendor number.

ambiguities.description: Vendor TaxID uniqueness: The transcript states that vendors can have duplicate tax IDs (parent companies with multiple subsidiaries filing together, or accidental duplicates). However, it does not explicitly clarify whether TaxID can be completely absent/null on a vendor record, or whether a vendor always has some TaxID value even if it is not unique. Should the model mandate that every Vendor has a TaxID?

source_references.excerpt: Could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead?... You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

ambiguities.description: Vendor RiskTier population and current marking: The facilitator and Raj discuss that a vendor can accumulate multiple RiskReviews over time, and 'at most one is the current one.' However, the model does not explicitly capture which review is marked current or how the current review is identified. Is there a boolean flag on RiskReview, or is 'current' derived from metadata (e.g., most recent with completion status)? The model currently does not represent this derivation.

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: RiskReview sign-off status: The transcript mentions that a review must be 'signed off' and refers to a 'completed' review as a condition for active status, but the model does not include explicit value types or constraints to capture the review's completion/sign-off status. Should RiskReview have a status field (e.g., draft, completed, signed) or other metadata indicating sign-off?

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review... At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Vendor address decomposition: The transcript mentions that vendors have three addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal), which are 'frequently different and frequently wrong,' but the model does not include separate facts for these address types. Should addresses be modeled as structured entities (e.g., separate fact types for each address role), or are they out of scope for this extraction?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Contact optionality by region: The transcript clarifies that 'If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all,' meaning a Vendor-Region combination may have no contact if the vendor doesn't operate there. However, the model does not formally express what happens when a Vendor DOES operate in a Region but has not yet assigned a contact. Is a contact mandatory for every Vendor-Region pair where the vendor operates?

source_references.excerpt: Can a vendor have no contact in a region?... If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all. Most of our vendors are one region only.

ambiguities.description: Vendor-to-PurchaseOrder direction: The fact type 'PurchaseOrder is raised against Vendor' models the one-to-many relationship (many POs per vendor, one vendor per PO). The transcript confirms a vendor can have many POs or none. However, it does not explicitly state whether the system enforces that a PO cannot exist without a vendor (only that the form won't create one that way). Should this be captured as strict referential integrity or a softer operational control?

source_references.excerpt: Can a vendor have many POs?... Many, or none. Plenty of vendors we onboarded and never used... You can't create one without picking a vendor. The form won't let you.

ambiguities.description: Suspension and in-flight POs: The transcript explicitly identifies an unresolved policy question: what happens to purchase orders already in flight when a vendor is suspended? The facilitator parks this as an undecided matter going to the sourcing steering group. The current model captures only the creation-time control (active vendors only) and does not model any post-suspension behavior. This is intentional per the facilitator's summary, but stakeholders should confirm this gap is acceptable for the current scope.

source_references.excerpt: If we suspend a vendor -- their review lapses, or there's a breach, or they turn up on a sanctions list -- what happens to the purchase orders already in flight?... Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Spend tier vs. Risk tier terminology collision: The transcript documents significant confusion where both 'spend tier' and 'risk tier' are colloquially called just 'tier' by stakeholders, leading to miscommunication. While the model now has distinct fact types (Vendor has SpendTier and Vendor has RiskTier), stakeholders have not formalized a naming convention to prevent future confusion in user-facing systems. This is noted as a known pain point but not formally resolved in this session.

source_references.excerpt: You both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos. Someone says 'that's a high tier vendor' in a meeting and half the room hears 'big spender' and the other half hears 'dangerous'... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: RiskTier value constraint application: The model captures RiskTier as a value type with values ['low', 'medium', 'high'], but the transcript does not explicitly state whether these are the ONLY possible values or if there are edge cases (e.g., 'unreviewed'). The current model assumes these three are complete and mutually exclusive.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high... based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

ambiguities.description: Vendor contact history: The transcript does not clarify whether vendor contacts change over time and whether historical changes should be tracked, or if only the current primary contact matters. The model assumes current-state only.

source_references.excerpt: I keep a spreadsheet... who the real contact is when the system contact is stale...

ambiguities.description: PurchaseOrder amount and date optionality: The transcript does not explicitly confirm whether a PurchaseOrder must always have both an amount and a raised date at creation, or whether these can be null/omitted initially. The model assumes both are present but does not formally mandate them.

source_references.excerpt: It has an amount and a raised date... I'll take vendor, number, amount, date and we can extend later.

ambiguities.description: Region code scope: The transcript mentions that there has been 'talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.' The model captures the current four regions as fixed via a value constraint, but this may need revision if organizational changes occur. Should the region set be treated as fixed or as a reference table that can evolve?

source_references.excerpt: Four regions, fixed?... Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.
